# Message Gateway: agent install instructions

You are an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, or similar) with shell
access. A user asked you to install Message Gateway, a self-hosted gateway for
sending email, SMS and push notifications through one API.

Your job has three parts, in this order:

  1. DOWNLOAD the project
  2. INSTALL and start it
  3. OPEN the setup page in the user's default browser

The user then finishes setup in their browser. Do not ask them for API keys,
passwords or any other secret in this chat, and do not create a `.env` file.

## 0. Prerequisites

Run these two checks:

    git --version
    docker info

- `git` missing: tell the user to install git, then stop.
- `docker` missing: tell the user to install Docker Desktop
  (https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/), start it, and tell you when
  it is running. Stop until they do.
- Docker installed but "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon": ask the user to
  start Docker Desktop and wait until it says it is running, then re-check.
- Do not try to install git or Docker yourself.

On Windows, run the commands below in WSL or Git Bash (the installer is a bash
script). Docker Desktop must be running.

## 1. Download

Clone into the user's home directory (or the folder they named, if they gave
one):

    git clone https://github.com/tadeubanzato/message-gateway ~/message-gateway
    cd ~/message-gateway

- If `~/message-gateway` already exists, do not clone again: `cd` into it and run
  `git pull`.
- If the clone fails with an authentication or "repository not found" error, the
  repository is private and the user needs GitHub access. Tell them to run
  `gh auth login` (or otherwise sign in to GitHub), then retry. Do not work
  around it.

## 2. Install

    ./install.sh

This builds the container (the first build takes a few minutes; be patient),
starts it, waits until it reports healthy, and then tries to open the setup page
in the default browser. There is nothing to configure first.

- If the port is busy, run `MG_PORT=9000 ./install.sh` and use that port in the
  steps below instead of 8010.
- If it fails, show the user the relevant lines it printed, fix the cause (Docker
  not running, port in use), and run it again. Do not retry in a loop.
- `./install.sh` is safe to run again: it rebuilds and restarts and keeps data.

## 3. Open the setup page in the user's default browser

`./install.sh` ends with one of these lines. Read your command output:

- "Opened the setup page in your default browser: http://localhost:8010"
  Good, nothing more to do for this step.
- "Could not open a browser automatically. Open this address yourself: ..."
  Try to open it for the user with the command for their system:

      macOS:        open http://localhost:8010
      Linux:        xdg-open http://localhost:8010
      Windows/WSL:  cmd.exe /c start "" http://localhost:8010

  If you are running somewhere the user's browser can't be reached (a remote
  machine, container or cloud sandbox), do not try further. Give the user the
  address and ask them to open it.

## 4. Hand over to the user

Tell the user, in your own words:

    Message Gateway is running. I've opened http://localhost:8010 in your
    browser. Finish setup there. It takes a couple of minutes:
      1. Storage: keep the data on this computer (default), or use MongoDB Atlas.
      2. Create the administrator account. The administrator can change all
         settings, connect and add email / SMS / push providers, and manage API
         keys.
      3. Save your API key. It is shown only once.
    After that, connect your first channel from the Channels menu or the Home
    page (Email, SMS or Push). Every provider card links to that provider's
    sign-in page. For SMS through their own service, they pick "Custom API
    endpoint" (the default) and either paste a working curl command for it
    and click "Fill in from curl", or give the URL and a sample JSON body
    themselves. Each connected provider can also be turned on or off with a
    click, without disconnecting it. Moving from an older install? Settings
    has an "Import from an existing .env file" option. Their credentials are
    typed into the browser and stored encrypted. They never come through this
    chat.

Then wait for the user to say they are done. If they ask which provider to pick:
Pushover or ntfy for push (ntfy needs no account), Mailjet or SendGrid for email,
Twilio, Infobip or Sinch for SMS if they want a hosted provider (Custom API
endpoint if they already have their own SMS service).

## 5. Connect to the gateway (optional, after setup)

The last setup screen shows a `claude mcp add ...` command that contains the
user's own API key (using their real address - not `localhost`, unless that's
genuinely where the gateway runs). Tell the user to copy it from that screen and
run it in their own terminal, then restart Claude Code (or run `/mcp`). Do NOT
ask them to paste the key or token into this chat, and do not try to create or
guess a key yourself. The gateway's About page also has a short prompt they can
paste into any other MCP-capable agent instead of that command.

Once connected, the MCP tools work with the user's key: `send_push`,
`send_email`, `send_sms`, `send_test`, `send_notification` (any channel);
`list_providers`, `get_setup_status`, `get_setup_instructions`, `get_health`;
`list_recent_messages`, `get_message`, `list_delivery_attempts` (that account's
own messages only). The administrator's key also unlocks `check_provider_config`,
`get_queue_status`, `list_dead_letters` and `retry_dead_letter`. Connecting
providers, managing keys, changing settings and turning a provider on/off are
done in the web app only, never through MCP.

## 6. Verify

    curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8010/health

Expect `"ok":true`, `"db_ok":true` and `"data_persistent":true`. If
`data_persistent` is false, the data is not on a Docker volume and would be lost
when the container is removed; tell the user and re-run `./install.sh`. Report the
result. That is the end of the install.

## Notes for the agent

- Never ask the user to paste API keys, tokens or passwords into this chat, and
  never write secrets into any file.
- Do not create a `.env` file. Values in `.env` override what the user enters in
  the browser, and the pages could not change them.
- The gateway listens on localhost only. To reach it from another machine the
  user must change the port binding in `docker-compose.yml` after setup.
- Useful commands (run in ~/message-gateway):
    docker compose stop          stop it
    docker compose start         start it again
    docker compose logs gateway  see what is happening
    docker compose down -v       uninstall and DELETE local data and the
                                 encryption key. Only if the user asks
- With local storage, the data and the encryption key that protects saved
  credentials live in the `gateway_data` Docker volume. Suggest a backup if it
  matters to them.
- If the user cannot run Docker or a shell, stop and tell them to follow the
  manual steps in README.md.
